Distribution in Brazil: This species was noted in the Amazon region as Staurastrum donellii Kurt Förster (Förster 1963: Serra da Lua, Roraima State, fig. 5); Staurastrum pseudozonatum [var. minutum] f. rectum Kurt Förster & Eckert (Förster 1964: Rio das Femmeas, Tocantins State, fig. 6); Staurastrum donnellii var. simplex Croasdale & A. M. Scott (Scott & al. 1965: Vigia Municipality, Pará State, fig. 7); Staurastrum pseudozonatum var. minutissimum Kurt Förster (Förster 1969: “ Igarapé Mapiri ” and “ Lago Jurucuí ”, Santarém Municipality, Pará State, fig. 8) and the present study (Itirapina Municipality, São Paulo State, figs 1 - 4).

Distribution and habitat: — Cerradicola miottoae is only known from the eastern Rio Grande do Sul state (Fig. 3), occurring on fragmented rocky outcrops within the Pampa at approximately 114 m above sea level. Similar to all other species in the genus, C. miottoae grows in dry, open environments, specifically in the rocky outcrops of the Pampa (IBGE 2004). The new species was found on the slope of a granite hill between huge blocks of rock, where there is dense shrubby vegetation with some arboreal elements such as Agarista eucalyptoides (Cham. & Schltdl.) G. Don (“ criúva ”) and Butia odorata (Barb. Rodr.) Noblick & Lorenzi (“ butiá ”). The site also presents many species of Asteraceae, including Baccharis psiadioides (Less.) Joch. Müll., Baccharis sessiliflora Vahl, Radlkoferotoma cistifolium (Less.) Kuntze, and Fabaceae as Centrosema virginianum (L.) Benth., Collaea stenophylla (Hook. & Arn.) Benth., Mimosa bifurca Benth., Rhynchosia corylifolia Mart. ex Benth., and R. lineata Benth., Euphorbiaceae (Croton cuchillae-nigrae Croizat), Verbenaceae (Aloysia gratissima (Gillies & Hook.) Tronc.) Lamiaceae (Glechon marifolia Benth. and Salvia ovalifolia Benth.), Plantaginaceae (Scoparia ericacea Cham. & Schltdl.), Malvaceae (Abutilon malachroides A. St. - Hil. & Naudin and Wissadula glechomifolia (A. St. - Hil.) R. E. Fr.), and Convolvulaceae (Ipomoea uruguayensis Meisn. and Jacquemontia heterotricha O’Donell).
